# OSS IQ

> An open-source CLI tool that reads a Python or JavaScript project's dependencies and reports, for each package, a next action, version drift, known CVEs and maintenance state across the whole dependency graph. It proposes update plans and can apply them.

## What OSS IQ Does

OSS IQ is a Software Composition Analysis (SCA) tool for platform engineers and development teams. It goes beyond vulnerability scanning to evaluate dependencies as long-term engineering assets.

- Scans project manifest files (package.json with package-lock.json; pyproject.toml with uv.lock; pylock.toml; requirements.txt)
- Cross-references against public package registries (npm, PyPI), CVE databases, and GitHub repository signals
- Reports a next action per package, plus a repository-stability verdict (`retain`, `patch`, `refactor` or `evict`) built from exploit probability and upstream maintenance
- Supports JavaScript (npm) and Python (uv, pip lock, pip) ecosystems
- Outputs reports as terminal console, HTML, JSON, or a compact agent format
- Exposes the same decisions to coding agents through a SKILL.md and a local MCP server (`ossiq install skills`)
- Checks a package before adding it: `ossiq add <package>` shows CVEs, maintainer information and health warnings, then adds the package after you confirm. Critical warnings block the add unless you pass `--force`
- Findings never change the exit code; gate CI with your own check over the `ossiq export` JSON

## Install and log in

- Run without installing: `uvx ossiq status` (PyPI) or `npx @ossiq/cli status` (npm: a native binary for macOS, Linux glibc and Windows x64; no Python needed)
- Log in to GitHub once with `ossiq auth login` (one-time code; the token stays in the OS secret store) to raise the API limit from 60 to 5,000 requests per hour. In CI and containers, set `OSSIQ_GITHUB_TOKEN` instead

## Documentation

- [Getting Started](https://ossiq.dev/getting-started.html): Installation, first scan, and basic usage
- [Log in to GitHub](https://ossiq.dev/how-to/github-login.html): Device-flow login, CI tokens, and troubleshooting
- [Verifying a release](https://ossiq.dev/how-to/verifying-a-release.html): Check the signed SLSA build provenance of an installed artifact with `gh attestation verify`
- [Recommendations and Risk](https://ossiq.dev/recommendations.html): What each recommendation means, the evidence behind it, and what it costs when that evidence is missing or wrong
- [Explanation](https://ossiq.dev/explanation/index.html): How recommendations are made, repository stability, and concepts
- [Reference](https://ossiq.dev/reference.html): Full CLI reference and configuration options
- [Tutorials](https://ossiq.dev/tutorials/): Step-by-step guides for common use cases

## Research & Analysis

- [OSS IQ Journal](https://ossiq.dev/journal/): In-depth reports on software supply chain risk and AI-assisted development
- [The Poisoned Well: How AI Amplifies Open Source Supply Chain Attacks](https://ossiq.dev/journal/the-poisoned-well-ai-supply-chain-attacks.html): Technical synthesis of supply-chain attack patterns, the AI amplification mechanisms (slopsquatting, agentic installs), and a defense-in-depth maturity model
- [The Hidden Cost of AI-Generated Code](https://ossiq.dev/journal/the-hidden-cost-of-ai-generated-code.html): Why faster AI-assisted code writing is degrading code quality, security, and delivery stability

## Sample Reports

- [npm scan example](https://ossiq.dev/_static/samples/scan_npm.html): Example output for a JavaScript project
- [PyPI scan example](https://ossiq.dev/_static/samples/scan_pypi.html): Example output for a Python project
